facts: Mobileye's Q2 2026 Form 10-Q says OEM sourcing and nomination can provide visibility two to three years in advance, but OEMs do not contractually commit to particular purchase volumes and program timing or volumes can change.

The Q2 2026 Form 10-Q says Mobileye co-developed multiple EyeQ generations with STMicroelectronics and has sought supply-chain redundancy, including an agreement for TSMC to manufacture imaging-radar components and some future EyeQ generations and potentially other future products.

Mobileye's 2025 Form 10-K reports that its solutions were installed in approximately 1,400 vehicle models, its SoCs had been deployed in more than 230 million vehicles, and it was actively working with more than 50 OEMs worldwide as of December 27, 2025.

The 2025 Form 10-K states that after the Mentee Robotics share issuance Intel beneficially owned approximately 77.0% of Mobileye's outstanding common stock and 96.9% of voting power as of February 3, 2026, leaving Intel able to control stockholder matters and subjecting specified major corporate actions to Intel consent while its ownership remains above the stated threshold.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Mobileye documents active supplier diversification beyond STMicroelectronics through TSMC for imaging-radar components and future EyeQ generations, improving redundancy while preserving material foundry dependence.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: A large installed base and multi-year OEM sourcing visibility support execution planning, but purchase volumes are not contractually committed and semiconductor manufacturing remains partner-dependent.

factors.name: governancePower
factors.basis: Intel retained approximately 96.9% voting power as of February 3, 2026 and can control stockholder matters and specified major corporate actions.

factors.name: thesisQuality
factors.basis: The approximately 1,400-model / 230-million-vehicle installed footprint and work with more than 50 OEMs support a scaled ADAS thesis, while non-binding future OEM volumes limit certainty about conversion.

risks: OEM sourcing visibility is not equivalent to committed purchase volume; timing and volume can change before revenue realization.
Supply diversification reduces single-supplier exposure but does not eliminate dependence on external semiconductor manufacturers.
Intel's concentrated voting control materially limits Class A holder influence and creates controlling-shareholder governance risk.
contradictions: Multi-year OEM program visibility can look like a contracted backlog, but Mobileye explicitly states OEMs do not commit to particular volumes and programs can change in timing and volume.
Supplier diversification improves resilience, but it should not be interpreted as vertically integrated semiconductor control because production remains dependent on external foundries and partners.
unknowns: The filing does not quantify what share of future EyeQ or radar production will be allocated to TSMC versus other suppliers.
The filing does not convert OEM nominations into contractually committed future revenue, so Alpha should not treat program visibility as backlog.
